For \(T'=19\): 37 stamps in 37 nonempty groups forces all groups to be singletons, impossible since not all stamps have value 19.

For \(T'=37\): the group containing 36 must be \(\{36,1\}\), then the group containing 35 must be \(\{35,2\}\), and so on down to \(\{19,18\}\), leaving \(\{37\}\). This is the only possibility, so there is \(1\) way.

For \(T'=703\): all stamps in one group, \(1\) way.

Thus the total number of ways is \(1+1=2\).

\[
\boxed{2}
\]
